newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bond yields breached the psychological 15 percent level on late Monday afternoon selling as the local market moved in sympathy with weaker U.S. Treasuries.
"It's in line with the U.S. market and expectations throughout the day that we would break through the figure. We've seen selling from all quarters," a trader at a leading bank said.

The 30-year U.S. T-bond was last trading at a 6.85 percent yield amid worries that U.S. National Association of Purchasing Managers data later on Monday could elicit more hawkish comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
At 1445 GMT government's benchmark R150 stock was trading at a 15.050 percent yield from 14.915 percent late on Friday.
Traders said early activity had been fairly volatile with the yield on the R150 see-sawing between around 14.86 percent to 14.95 percent.
The tone in the market was uncertain, they said, ahead of the March 12 budget.
"The market is a little confused, still reeling from the poor money supply and private credit extension figures last week and nervous ahead of the budget," another trader commented.
There was room for more weakness, possibly up to the 15.15 percent level in the immediate future, he added.
Bond Exchange statistics show foreigners bought a net 207.26 million rands worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 100.54 million on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 11.73 billion rand.
On the currency market, the rand lingered in the doldrums. It moved slightly firmer during the late morning session only to idle around the 4.47 level for the rest of the day.
At 1445 GMT it was at 4.4735/4765 on the dollar from 4.4755/85 last on Friday.
"Blame the day's inactivity on the cricket...most people focused on the SA-Australian cricket match," one forex trader said.
Others noted that one- and two-month rand volatilities had moved higher from last week in what appeared to be players hedging themselves ahead of the March 12 budget.
"The focus is definitely the budget," another trader said.

Dealers noted there was some interest in the successful bidder for a 30 percent stake in telecommunications utility Telkom, particularily in the amount of flows into the country the sale would generate and how these would affect the market.
After the official South African market close, the government announced that it planned to sell a 30 percent stake in Telkom to a consortium of SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd.
Analysts have estimated the value of the 30 percent stake at over six billion rand, valuing Telkom at more than $4 billion.

Forex traders expected that rand to maintain a 4.46 to 4.49 range over the next few days and said the Reserve Bank was still sitting on the offering side, ready to defend the unit from a move above the 4.50 level.
Against the crosses the rand was last quoted at 7.2390/2483 on sterling from 7.2862/2964 and at 0.3781/3786 marks from 0.3777/3780.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates held unchanged between 16.50 and 16.70 percent. The 90-day BA rate was also unmoved at between 15.90 and 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.736 billion rand on Saturday from 8.823 billion rand on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
